In a verifier configured with both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms in `algorithms=[…]` and a raw-JSON JWK as the key, an attacker could forge HS256 tokens using the JWK text as the HMAC secret. Simplify the test suite decorators

#12502: The UX of the GitHub automation making pull requests to update the plugin list has been updated. Previously, the maintainers had to close the automatically created pull requests and re-open them to trigger the CI runs. From now on, they only need to click the [Ready for review]{.title-ref} button instead.
\#14303: The documentation is now built with Sphinx \>= 9.
Complete type hinting of jwks_client.py (#578) by @jdufresne

\#7255: The pytest\_warning\_captured <\_pytest.hookspec.pytest\_warning\_captured> hook is deprecated in favor of pytest\_warning\_recorded <\_pytest.hookspec.pytest\_warning\_recorded>, and will be removed in a future version.
`pytest_report_header`{.interpreted-text role="hook"} - the `startdir` parameter - use `start_path` instead.
Export `PyJWK` and `PyJWKSet` #652
`pytest.MarkGenerator` for the `pytest.mark `{.interpreted-text role="class"} singleton.
Remove algorithm requirement for JWT API
Special shout out to @jdufresne for all the amazing work getting this project into tip-top shape.

\#9488: If custom subclasses of nodes like `pytest.Item`{.interpreted-text role="class"} override the `init` method, they should take `kwargs`. See `uncooperative-constructors-deprecated`{.interpreted-text role="ref"} for details.
This release bundles five security fixes plus three additional hardening / spec-compliance changes.
The affected features will be effectively removed in pytest 9.1, so please consult the `deprecations` section in the docs for directions on how to update existing code.

text: \#5095: XML files of the `xunit2` family are now validated against the schema by pytest\'s own test suite to avoid future regressions.
This is the Jinja 3.1.4 security release, which fixes security issues and bugs but does not otherwise change behavior and should not result in breaking changes.
Run pyupgrade to simplify code and use Python 3.6 syntax (#536) by @jdufresne
